title: పక్కింటి వెంకీ మామ – ఎపిసోడ్ 1: ఒకే వీధి, రెండు బిల్లులు (Pakkinti Venky Mama, Ep. 1)
logline: Sweaty Subbarao wages a ridiculous war on his electricity bill (fridge-hugging, candle dinner, the AC remote kept garlanded in the showcase "for guests only", a stethoscope on the neighbour's meter) while next-door Venky Mama lives in monkey-cap AC comfort under his solar panels; one desperate "మామా... ఎలా?!" over the parapet, a silent point-up at the panels, and a deadpan wife ("ఇక చాలు. నేను కాల్ చేశా.") later, Subbarao hugs his own new solar panel exactly the way he hugged his fridge, and the angry little bill mascot ends up inside an avakaya jar.
humor_style: Escalating neighbour-envy contrast comedy in the Godavari "pakkinti vaadu" tradition, cut like a tennis match every ~2.4 s with a record-scratch colour snap on every A/B cut (Subbarao's world is cold, desaturated and sweaty; Venky's world is warm, golden and smug). Deadpan third-person Telugu captions do the talking so it works muted; the jokes are visual first (fridge hug, candle dinner, garlanded remote in the showcase, vadiyalu beside the panels, stethoscope on a yawning meter). A recurring HTML mascot, బిల్లుగాడు (a moustachioed angry paper bill sticker), rides Subbarao's shoulder in every A-side frame and gets his comeuppance in a pickle jar. Structural callback: fridge hug -> panel hug; split screen at the start rhymes with split screen at the turn. Affectionate, never cruel: Subbarao is lovable, Venky is friendly-smug, Lakshmi is the competent decision-maker, and the only villain is the bill.
why_it_spreads: Every street in Kakinada has a Venky Mama and every family has a Subbarao, so the caption invites tagging ("మీ వీధిలో సుబ్బారావు ఎవరు?"). The fridge hug plus a red number stops the thumb in one second and the whole premise ("ఒకే వీధి. ఒకే ఎండ. రెండు బిల్లులు.") is stated by 3 s with sound off. Each gag is shared middle-class memory (candle dinner, AC "for guests only", last guest 2019 Sankranti, vadiyalu drying on the roof, snooping on the neighbour's meter) and every frame is a different image with its own colour world, so there is no "same photo" feeling. The A/B rhythm plus the two rhyming split screens keep retention; the fridge-hug -> panel-hug bookend loops cleanly; "= నెలకు 20 బిర్యానీలు" is the quotable line; బిల్లుగాడు in the avakaya jar is the screenshot; the phone numbers arrive as the wife's punchline rather than a bolted-on ad; and "వెంకీ మామ ఎపిసోడ్ 2 కమింగ్ సూన్" frames it as a series from day one.

risks: Character consistency across 12 images: generate the four REFERENCE_PROMPT portraits first with Canva generate-image, then make every other shot as an image-reference edit from that portrait, keeping the clothing lines verbatim in every prompt. Expect 2-3 generations per shot; do a contact sheet of all 12 stills side by side before any animation and reject any frame where a face drifts (the owner's 'who is this new man' complaint is the mirror image of 'same photo').

Four two-person frames remain (3: Subbarao + Lakshmi, 5: Subbarao + Chinnu, 11: Subbarao + Chinnu, 12: Subbarao + Venky). Plan the composite fallback from the start: generate each person separately against the same background, Canva remove-background, layer in the HTML timeline; or split the frame into two comic panels. Shot 11 can ship with Subbarao alone and the 'AC ఆన్!' burst sticker carrying Chinnu's cheer.

Prop frames most likely to fail: the stethoscope on the meter (7; fallback: ear pressed flat to the box), the garlanded remote in the showcase (5; fallback: remote under a small glass dome on the TV stand with the garland added as a sticker), the monkey cap and blanket (4; fallback: blanket only, cap as a sticker). Generated meter must be generic grey with a blank display; the HTML counter masks the display regardless and must crawl, never stop or read zero.

Claims: every rupee figure (₹3,200*, ₹700*, ₹800*, 20 biryanis*) carries a visible asterisk and the '3 kW నమూనా' footnote so the sample is internally consistent (the earlier ₹4,870 -> ₹900 pairing implied a larger system than a PM Surya Ghar 3 kW sample); the end disclaimer is on screen for at least 2.8 s above the bottom 250 px. Never let a sticker say 'zero bill', 'guaranteed', 'subsidy approved' or imply unlimited AC; 'AC ఆన్... టెన్షన్ ఆఫ్' replaces 'mini Shimla' and the 18 C counter on purpose.

No DISCOM anywhere: Subbarao snoops on the meter himself; there is no meter reader, lanyard, ledger or ID card, so no utility staff is mocked. If the generator draws any utility-like logo, lettering or a house number, regenerate.
Vadiyalu must stay on the cloth on the terrace floor, never on the panel glass; check shot 6 and regenerate if anything touches the panels.

Text density rule for muted viewing: never more than two readable Telugu text blocks on screen at once; shots 5, 10, 11 and 12 are staggered as specified; name tags were cut from shots 1-2 (Venky's name arrives via the ₹700* pill, Subbarao's only in shot 7). Wrap every Telugu fragment in the Noto Sans Telugu class; Telugu inside a Poppins-first stack renders broken.

Timeline is 28.6 s at 30 fps using the skill's deterministic seek engine (all CSS animations with absolute delays, animation-play-state paused, JS counters inside seek). Render a test contact sheet every ~2 s and look at it before the full render; check the two split screens, bubbles vs. faces, the counter vs. footnote, and the end card vs. the disclaimer.

No voice-over by design; synthesized SFX (sting, whoosh, record scratch, ding, boing, pop, cash register) are made with ffmpeg and mixed about 6 dB under the trending audio the owner adds later, so the hits still read without fighting the track. Deliver with the SFX-only mix and a muted version.

Tone: Subbarao is lovable not stupid, Venky is friendly-smug, Lakshmi is the competent decision-maker (not a nagging-wife stereotype), Chinnu is always grinning. All people are fictional AI-generated characters; do not reuse any real customer's face or name. The street-lamp homework gag was cut for production risk (night + child + two people) and is parked for Episode 2 along with the fan-speed-1 dial and the flying chappal.

Instagram operations: verify the bio link actually points to the savings calculator before posting; someone must reply to 'SOLAR' comments within hours; repost as a Story with a link sticker (the only tappable link). The optional real-calculator phone mock in the end card needs the local-serve Playwright route from the kinetic-reel skill; if that is not set up, ship the orange button.
